introduction:
My research focuses on spatial computing and mixed reality, particularly how spatial representation and affordance-aware mapping can support interactions across different physical environments.

Building on this foundation, I am exploring how spatial configurations and human activities shape shared MR experiences, with a growing interest in how AI can support context-aware and adaptive interactions.

cvAbout:
I am a **Ph.D. student** in the **Graduate School of Culture Technology at KAIST**, advised by **Prof. Woontack Woo** in the **Ubiquitous Virtual Reality Lab**.

My research focuses on **spatial computing and mixed reality**, with an emphasis on **spatial representation**, **affordance-aware mapping**, and interaction across heterogeneous physical environments.

More recently, I have been exploring how **spatial configurations and social contexts** influence experiences in shared MR. I am interested in extending this work toward intelligent systems that can understand spatial and activity contexts and support **adaptive interactions**.

**I am currently seeking postdoctoral opportunities** to further pursue this research direction.
researchVision: From enabling spatial correspondence to understanding and supporting collaboration within shared environments.

researchThemes.title: Spatial Representation and Mapping
researchThemes.description: I develop scene-graph representations and geometric mapping methods that capture semantic relationships and spatial affordances. My published work on Geometric Spatial Affordance Graphs, object-cluster registration, and affine mapping establishes correspondences between heterogeneous physical environments while preserving opportunities for interaction.

researchThemes.title: Human-Centered Shared Mixed Reality
researchThemes.description: Building on these spatial foundations, I investigate how physical constraints and interpersonal spatial relationships shape distributed MR collaboration. This direction examines spatial configurations, proxemics, and F-formations in relation to social presence, co-presence, and collaborative behavior.

researchThemes.title: Spatially Aware Human-AI Interaction
researchThemes.description: I am interested in how machine-interpretable spatial representations could establish shared context between people and AI agents. Future questions include how assistance might account for human activities, environmental constraints, and social relationships to support adaptive interaction and human-AI coordination in shared environments.

publicationHighlights.object-cluster: Matching individual objects can miss the relationships that make a space usable. Geometric Spatial Affordance Graphs and Object Cluster Registration align groups of objects across dissimilar rooms to preserve multi-object interaction in shared virtual spaces.
publicationHighlights.affine-spaces: Dissimilar layouts make continuous spatial correspondence difficult. Spatial affordance-aware affine patches align interaction zones and object relationships, supporting object matching and user movement across shared MR spaces.
publicationHighlights.subspace-allocation: A common overlap can shrink as more remote users join. Separating perceivable space from each user's interactable subspace supports a shared view while allocating interaction areas suited to different physical layouts.
publicationHighlights.mutual-space: Different spatial matching methods use incompatible representations. A proposed mutual-space representation brings physical space, spatial matching, and collaboration context into a common structure to support their integrated use in remote MR collaboration.
